content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain white bread is made from whole wheat where the bran and germ are retained. It has a soft white crumb, a light crust, and a mildly sweet flavor. This bread is suitable for everyday consumption and works well for sandwiches, toast, and as a side.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain bread contains more fiber and nutrients than regular white bread.
Dough made with whole grain flour requires longer kneading and proofing times.
The white crumb is achieved by using the lighter part of the grain and a small amount of sugar.
In many countries whole grain bread is considered a staple of healthy eating.
When properly wrapped, the bread can stay fresh for up to 5 days at room temperature.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B3 and B6 vitamins aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The bread provides magnesium, iron and zinc, essential for muscle function and immunity.

items.title: Lower glycemic index
items.content: Compared with refined white bread, whole grain varieties cause a slower rise in blood glucose.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Phytonutrients in whole grains help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease may experience severe reactions after eating the bread.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Gluten can be problematic for those following a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although healthier, the bread still provides calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties are salty; individuals with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bread fresh, toasted, or as the base for sandwiches, wraps, soups and salads. It pairs well with avocado, low‑fat cheese, turkey, vegetables and nut butters.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in a paper bag or cloth sack at room temperature to keep the crust crisp. For longer storage, keep it in an airtight container in the refrigerator (up to 7 days) or freeze (up to 3 months). Thaw and warm before serving.
